summary: Ad-hoc request: incremental S3 lakehouse delivery with opaque-tenant encapsulation and RFC3161 timestamped manifest
description: Customer requests an on-demand, incremental export from our audit stream into their S3 lakehouse. Deliverables must meet two specific constraints: (1) each S3 partition file must be wrapped in an opaque tenant envelope (customer manages tenant decryption) so raw tenant identifiers are never exposed in storage; (2) each incremental checkpoint must include an RFC3161-compliant timestamp token (time-stamp authority proof) and an accompanying SHA-256 manifest for non-repudiation. They also want an optionally signed KMS-wrapped key proof to show the envelope integrity was produced by Redwood's KMS.
impact: Customer requires this bundle for an upcoming regulatory evidence submission. Delay > 5 business days will block their audit timeline and may escalate to legal review. No production API outage reported; this is an evidence/delivery request with medium urgency.
request_details:
- Delivery cadence: hourly incremental deltas for the previous 24 hours as a single zipped bundle delivered to their customer-owned S3 bucket (s3://vaultbridge-evidence/redwood/).
- File layout: partitioned by year/month/day/hour with each file named <checkpoint_id>.<sha256>.enc.zip and accompanied by <checkpoint_id>.rfc3161.tst
- Tenant encapsulation: payload must be tenant-encrypted (opaque envelope). Redwood should not store the tenant decryption key; include envelope metadata that indicates KMS-key-id used and an HMAC over envelope with Redwood's signing key.
- RFC3161 timestamp: request includes a TSP token per checkpoint, signed by a recognized TSA. Customer provided example TSA: https://tsa.example.com
- Manifest: top-level manifest.json listing files, sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and RFC3161 token identifiers. Manifest must be checksumed and included in the signed bundle.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer provided a sample event range (2026-03-08T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z) and sample bucket details.
2) Customer reports inability to map our standard audit export to their opaque-envelope format using the public docs (they need Redwood to produce the encapsulation at the source prior to S3 delivery).
3) Support should validate whether the export pipeline can insert an envelope layer and attach RFC3161 tokens per checkpoint.
observed_logs: Customer submitted a sample delivery log (delivery-log-20260309.txt) showing successful PutObject calls but missing envelope metadata and missing .rfc3161 tokens. Excerpt: 'PUT s3://vaultbridge-evidence/redwood/2026/03/08/00/checkpoint-0001.zip 200 OK' with no additional metadata headers. They attached CloudTrail and delivery receipts.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: export pipeline currently supports JSON and Parquet partitioning with optional server-side encryption (SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS) but no opaque-tenant envelope abstraction at the object level.
Checked ingestion worker logs for hourly export jobs between 2026-03-08 00:00 and 2026-03-09 00:00: no evidence of envelope metadata injection. Worker version: export-service v1.12.4.

KMS: Redwood KMS keys available to support team. Need to confirm whether we can sign HMACs with existing service signing key or must route to dedicated evidence-signing KMS key (policy/legal constraint).
RFC3161: Our internal time-stamp service can generate RFC3161 tokens but currently not automatically attached to export checkpoints; requires TSP integration and packaging step (backend change).

Hypothesis: Deliverable requires a short-lived packaging job that pulls delta files, wraps each payload in the envelope format, requests RFC3161 token from TSA, generates manifest, signs manifest with KMS-signing key, and pushes zipped bundle to customer S3 with appropriate ACL and object metadata.
Potential blockers: cross-account S3 put permissions for their bucket, TSA whitelisting / fees, creation of a new packaging job with KMS-signing key and audit trail.

resolution: 2026-03-12: Agreed next steps with customer: (A) Redwood will deliver a one-off prototype packaging job for the requested sample window within 5 business days; (B) packaging job will write to a pre-authorized, customer-owned S3 path and include per-checkpoint RFC3161 token and a signed manifest (signed with a dedicated evidence-signing KMS key after legal approval); (C) customer will supply tenant decryption public info and TSA service details.

Workaround: For immediate needs, customer can continue to ingest full audit export and run tenant encapsulation internally. Support provided mapping guidance and a sample Python script to perform envelope wrapping and generate RFC3161 tokens using their TSA.
Follow-up actions: create INT-40211 (internal task) to prototype packaging job; security to review KMS key policy and legal to prepare amendment; engineering estimate due by 2026-03-17.
